**How to submit:** Write on paper and show your steps. Upload a clear photo to the university e-learning platform. Due: **before lecture 2**.
No task needs AI. The optional Task with AI at the end gives no marks.

## Task 1 · The grid (2 marks)

The centre of a level is the origin; x goes right and y goes up. A key is 5
units left of the centre and 3 units down.

a) Write the position of the key and its quadrant. (1 mark)

{{< answer-space lines=1 >}}

b) The player is at (2, 4). Write the vector from the player to the key. Use
end − start. (1 mark)

{{< answer-space lines=2 >}}

## Task 2 · A patrol (3 marks)

A robot starts at (−6, 3) and must reach (6, −5) in 4 frames, with the same
velocity in every frame.

a) Find the velocity. Show your steps. (1 mark)

{{< answer-space lines=2 >}}

b) Write the positions after frames 1, 2, 3 and 4. (1 mark)

{{< answer-space lines=2 >}}

c) Draw the five positions (frames 0 to 4) on squared paper. Are they on one
straight line? (1 mark)

{{< answer-space box=5 >}}

## Optional · Task with AI (no marks) {.extra}

::: {.callout-note .ai-task title="Task with AI · Draw a robot's patrol"}
An extra for the curious: let an AI assistant draw it. Copy the prompt
into an AI assistant that the university allows (for example Microsoft
Copilot with your university account), and look at the picture.

::: {.prompt}
Draw a 2D grid with x and y from −6 to 10, with numbered axes. A robot
starts at (−4, −2) and must reach (8, 4) in 3 frames, with the same
velocity in every frame. Draw its position after frames 0, 1, 2 and 3 as
dots, write the frame number next to each dot, and write the velocity.
:::

**What do you see?**

::: {.check label="What you should see"}
Four dots on one straight line: (−4, −2), (0, 0), (4, 2) and (8, 4). The
velocity is (4, 2): the whole move (12, 6) divided by 3 frames.
:::

::: {.try-change}
**Change:** let the robot take 6 frames instead of 3, and ask again. What do you
notice?

::: {.check}
Seven dots on the same line, closer together: the velocity is (2, 1), half
as big, because the same move is split into twice as many frames.
:::
:::

::: {.try-change}
**Change:** let the robot reach (8, −2) in 3 frames, and ask again. What do you
notice?

::: {.check}
The dots are on a flat line: (−4, −2), (0, −2), (4, −2), (8, −2). The
velocity is (4, 0): the robot only moves to the right.
:::
:::

**Your own idea:** change one more number or word, and look again. The AI
can be wrong: compare its result with the answers.
:::
